subsystems.name: Rules library
subsystems.role: the written regulations turned into machine-readable logic.

subsystems.name: City data layer
subsystems.role: the evidence compliance is checked against.

subsystems.name: Compliance engine
subsystems.role: applies the rules to the data and flags what fails.

subsystems.name: Interface layer
subsystems.role: how officials, developers and residents see and contest results.

buildSteps.title: Audit the rulebook
buildSteps.detail: Planners list every regulation a development must satisfy and note which are already machine-checkable and which need human judgement.

buildSteps.title: Encode the rules
buildSteps.detail: Ordinary language is translated into formal rules — often as geometry and attribute checks against a BIM model or a map layer.

buildSteps.title: Connect the data
buildSteps.detail: Permit systems, GIS, building models and sensor feeds are linked through standard interfaces so the engine can read them automatically.

buildSteps.title: Build the compliance engine
buildSteps.detail: The rules run against each submission; machine learning catches anomalies (an unpermitted structure, a pollutant spike) that fixed rules miss.

buildSteps.title: Log every decision
buildSteps.detail: Each check and its outcome is recorded with who or what made it, so a decision can be explained and appealed.

buildSteps.title: Pilot on one process
buildSteps.detail: A single high-volume workflow — say, solar-panel or small-extension permits — is automated first and compared against manual review.

buildSteps.title: Scale and keep it current
buildSteps.detail: Roll out to more permit types, and keep the rules library synced as codes change.

prerequisites.tech: Digitised municipal records and open APIs
prerequisites.why: the engine can only check what it can read; many cities still run on paper and PDFs.

prerequisites.tech: BIM and open standards such as IFC
prerequisites.why: gives buildings a structured, machine-readable description that rules can be tested against.
provides live environmental data to check ongoing compliance, not just designs.
compliance monitoring touches personal and commercial data and must not become surveillance.
a permit refusal has to be justified in terms a citizen or court can follow.

pathway.milestone: e-permitting and automated pre-checks in a minority of cities
pathway.unlocks: shorter approval times and fewer clerical errors.

pathway.milestone: BIM-based automated code checking adopted in mainstream planning
pathway.unlocks: designs corrected before submission rather than after.

pathway.milestone: live compliance monitoring from city sensors and digital twins
pathway.unlocks: catching breaches as they happen instead of at annual inspection.
portable systems, so smaller municipalities can adopt them affordably.
